prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stocks with a Shot at Beating the S&P 500

No one can reliably pick stocks that beat the S&P 500 over a given year. S&P's SPIVA reports consistently find that most professional large-cap fund managers underperform the index, and over 10–15 years roughly 85–90% of them do. So treat this as a list of well-reasoned bets, not a forecast.

Also, my information only runs through about May 2026, and I don't have live prices. Check current valuations and recent news before buying anything.

## The List

| # | Company (Ticker) | Why it could outperform | Key risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Nvidia (NVDA)** | Dominant AI accelerator platform, with a software moat (CUDA) and very strong margins | Big customers designing their own chips, China export limits, cyclical spending |
| 2 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Makes nearly all advanced AI chips for Nvidia, Apple, AMD and others. Not in the S&P 500, so it adds real differentiation | Taiwan geopolitical risk, tariffs |
| 3 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Custom AI chips for hyperscalers like Google, plus AI networking and VMware software cash flow | Depends on a few large customers; rich valuation |
| 4 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Search cash machine, fast-growing Google Cloud, its own TPU chips, Gemini, Waymo. Often cheaper than its mega-cap peers | Antitrust remedies, AI disrupting search |
| 5 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Azure growth, AI built into Office and enterprise software, very durable business | Heavy AI spending needs to pay off |
| 6 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS, a high-margin ad business, and improving retail profitability | Capex intensity, consumer slowdown |
| 7 | **Meta (META)** | Best-in-class ad targeting improved by AI, huge user base, strong cash generation | Large AI/metaverse spending, regulation |
| 8 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | GLP-1 leader (Mounjaro/Zepbound) with an oral pill (orforglipron) in the pipeline. A growth driver outside tech | Drug-pricing policy, competition, high valuation |
| 9 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Gas turbines, grid equipment, and electrification, which data centers need for power. Large order backlog | Already priced for strong growth; wind segment execution |
| 10 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Best-run large US bank, benefits from dealmaking and trading activity. Diversifies away from tech | Credit cycle or recession |

## Why this mix
- **Themes:** The list leans into AI infrastructure (chips, cloud, power) because that's where earnings growth has been strongest. It adds healthcare (LLY) and financials (JPM) so it isn't purely a tech bet.
- **To beat the index, you have to be different from it.** NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META and AVGO are already large parts of the S&P 500. Holding them at 10% each is a concentrated bet on mega-cap tech continuing to lead. TSM, GEV and LLY at higher weights are where most of the differentiation comes from.

## The big caveat
This portfolio is **highly correlated**. If AI spending slows or sentiment turns, most of these stocks could fall together and trail the index by a wide margin. Concentration can beat the market, but it can also lose to it badly.

## Practical suggestions
1. **Core + satellite:** Keep most of your money in a low-cost S&P 500 index fund. Put a smaller portion (e.g., 10–30%) into picks like these. You get a shot at outperformance without betting everything on it.
2. **Size positions sensibly:** Equal-weight (10% each of the satellite portion) is a simple starting point.
3. **Measure honestly:** Track your picks against an S&P 500 ETF (e.g., SPY or VOO) over the year, including any trading costs and taxes.
4. **Check taxes:** In many countries, holding for more than a year gets better tax treatment. Rules vary by country, so check yours.
5. **Fit your situation:** Make sure this matches your time horizon, emergency savings, and risk tolerance. Consider talking to a licensed financial adviser, since I don't know your full circumstances.

If it would help, I can build a more aggressive or more defensive version of this list, or one that avoids overlap with the S&P 500 entirely.
